Introduction

The holy Archangel Gabriel is God’s messenger in Daniel and Luke and announces the Incarnation to the Theotokos.

Read the published life [1]

Death / martyrdom

Angelic messenger; no human death or martyrdom

Read circumstances and sources

An angelic messenger

Gabriel is an angelic servant of God rather than a human bishop, monk or martyr. Daniel names him when he is sent to explain a vision and again when he comes with understanding concerning the prophet’s prayer. The account presents his authority as received from God.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Daniel 8:15–19; 9:20–27

The Gospel announcements

Luke identifies Gabriel as the messenger who announces the birth of St. John the Baptist to the priest in the Temple. He then comes to Nazareth and announces to the Virgin Mary that she will bear Jesus, the Son of the Most High. His explanation of the Holy Spirit’s work belongs to the Gospel narrative of the Incarnation.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Luke 1:5–38

Angelic identity

A human birth date and death narrative do not apply to this profile. The biblical passages identify Gabriel as a heavenly messenger, so he should not be assigned a martyrdom, burial place or human succession.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Daniel 8:16; Luke 1:19,26

Orthodox commemoration

The OCA celebrates Archangel Gabriel’s Synaxis on March 26, immediately after the Annunciation, and also lists July 13. He is included with the heavenly powers on November 8. A synaxis is a liturgical assembly or commemoration; these observances honor God’s messenger in connection with the saving events he announces.

[1] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Opening explanation and final paragraph
